system.uid.note: Third ID word read from offset 0x14 (was 0x08, not part of the ID, RM0377 §28.2): fixed 2026-09-25, awaiting bench

system.recovery.note: No USB, so no ROM DFU path to park in

system.swo.note: Cortex-M0+ has no ITM/SWO; hal_debug_printf is a no-op

system.wamr.note: WAMR builds target the Cortex-M33 Cores only (Makefile WAMR_ENABLED guard); 2 KB SRAM

clocks.hsi.note: 'high': HSI16 in voltage range 1 at 0 WS (RM0377 Table 14). Bench 2026-09-26 (tests/hw-clock-levels, high): SysTick against HSI16 0 ppm.

clocks.msi.note: MSIRDY is bit 9 (RM0377 §7.3.1; the L0 used to poll bit 1 and hang at 'low'); SYSCLK_HZ carries the exact 1.048576 / 2.097152 MHz. Bench 2026-09-26 (tests/hw-clock-levels, low + medium): boots, range 3 / 2 at 0 WS, SYSCLK against HSI16 +3693 / +800 ppm.

clocks.pll.note: 'max': HSI16 x4 /2 = 32 MHz, VCO 64 MHz (limit 96 in range 1, RM0377 §7.2.4), range 1, 1 WS. Bench 2026-09-26 (tests/hw-clock-levels, max): 0 ppm against HSI16.

uart.lp.note: LPUART1 bus clock was never enabled (RCC_APB1ENR bit 18, RM0377 §7.3.14). Fixed 2026-09-25, awaiting bench

i2c.std.note: I2C1 kernel clock is HSI16 (RCC_CCIPR.I2C1SEL) at every clock level, so 100/400 kHz timing no longer depends on SYSCLK; bus recovery now uses PB6/PB7 (it drove PA9/PA10). 2026-09-25, awaiting bench

i2c.fast.note: 400 kHz at the MSI levels (the default project + an I2C tile failed to build: 'requires at least 4 MHz'); HSI16 kernel clock, restarted after Stop. 2026-09-25, awaiting bench

timer.wdog.note: Timeout from the measured LSI (ll_lsi_hz(), TIM21 capture against SYSCLK at the first core_watchdog_start) instead of a nominal 37 kHz on a 26-56 kHz part. Bench 2026-09-26 (tests/hw-lsi-cal T4/T5, all four levels): 5 s programmed within 0.2 % of the LSI implied by 10 RTC seconds, and a starved watchdog reset 5004-5014 ms later by the calibrated RTC; tests/hw-sleep-cycle: no resets across chunked Stops.

adc.raw.note: Asynchronous HSI16 ADC clock at the HSI16 levels; PCLK/2 with LFMEN below 3.5 MHz at the MSI levels (tiles#283). Bench 2026-09-26 (tests/hw-led-scale): VREFINT conversions at all four levels give VDD 3294-3298 mV on a 3.3 V rail.

adc.mv.note: VREFINT was never enabled on the L0 before 2026-09-22 (VREFEN written to reserved CFGR2 bits), so earlier readings were ~9x off. Fixed; VDDA reads 3294-3298 mV at all four clock levels on a ~3.3 V rail (2026-09-26, tests/hw-led-scale). Re-verify with known input voltages.

adc.temp.note: Reads sensor; factory cal at 0x1FF8007A — value offset needs investigation

adc.dma_mv.note: Scan-to-millivolt chain verified on silicon 2026-09-22; absolute accuracy not yet checked against known input voltages.

power.stop.note: LSE/LSI bit swap fixed (RM0377 §7.3.20), WUF cleared before each Stop, sleeps in fed chunks since the L0 IWDG runs in Stop, Alarm A's EXTI 17 masked during the sleep. Bench 2026-09-26 (tests/hw-sleep-cycle): two core_stop_for(10) with the 5 s watchdog running, 10 s each by the RTC and 10000 ms by SysTick, 0 watchdog resets.

power.standby.note: Same LSI fix as power.stop, plus WUTF cleared before entry (RM0377 Table 40). Refuses (HAL_ERROR) a Standby longer than half the watchdog timeout, since the L0 IWDG keeps running in Standby. Fixed 2026-09-25, awaiting bench

power.rtc_wake.note: RTC wakeup timer on LSI (ll_lsi_hz(), measured), EXTI line 20 + NVIC vector 2. Bench 2026-09-26 (tests/hw-sleep-cycle T3/T4).

power.exti_wake.note: core_stop_until_on_change waits for the pad edge itself, wakes to feed a running watchdog, returns at once if the pad is already at its wake level, and core_stop_until_on_change_timeout() bounds the wait (RTC-measured). 2026-09-25, awaiting bench

power.rtc_alarm.note: Alarm A (ALRMAR 0x1C, ALRAWF). Bench 2026-09-26 (tests/hw-sleep-cycle T2): ALRMAR reads back 0x80808003 and the alarm fired 2960 ms after it was set for xx:xx:03.

power.backup.note: 5 backup registers (RTC_BKP0R-4R at RTC+0x50, RM0377 §22.7.20). Bench 2026-09-26 (tests/hw-sleep-cycle T1, and progress kept across watchdog resets in tests/hw-lsi-cal).

adv.comp.note: L011 has COMP1/COMP2 but not routed on Core.ST.L0 pinout

nvm.eeprom.note: True data EEPROM, 512 B. Writes step from range 3 up to range 2 and back (RM0377 §6.1.4), check FLASH_SR (tiles#291) and read back; erased reads 0x00 (RM0377 §3.3.4). Bench 2026-09-26 (tests/hw-nvm-eeprom at low and max): range checks, erased state, 32-byte pattern, read_byte / write_byte (tiles#284), an injected SIZERR returns CORE_NVM_ERR_FLASH, boot counter across a reset.

nvm.otp.note: The STM32L011 has no OTP area (it has data EEPROM, see nvm.eeprom)
